content.text: The picture is clear. There's a shared `ProblemDetails.build` helper already used by several handlers (Validation, DataIntegrity, Forbidden, General). The rejection handlers for 400/409/429 still return plain `String`/`Map` bodies. Let me confirm which exception fires for the tested case (missing city) and check the POST owners pipeline.

content.content:
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Replay an already-seen Idempotency-Key as the original owner (200) before creating again.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkEmailDomain

# Reject a disposable-mail-provider email domain with 400 before any persistence.
checkEmailDomain:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckEmailDomain
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

# Validate an optional postcode against the city's region before any persistence.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidatePostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Assign householdId before the identity check so it forms part of the key. Household
# members with different telephones are admitted here and capped by MembershipLevel; the
# identity check below is the sole duplicate gate (see CheckUniqueIdentity).
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentity

checkIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckUniqueIdentity
  method: service
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagCapacityWarning

# Warn (does not reject) when the city already holds 40-49 owners, approaching the hard 50 limit.
flagCapacityWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagCapacityWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: adjustDate

adjustDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AdjustRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCode

assignCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: dedupeCode

# De-duplicate the assigned customerCode against existing owners: append '-<n>' with the
# smallest n >= 2 on collision, before the code is persisted.
dedupeCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DeduplicateCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagBulkSignup

flagBulkSignup:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagBulkSignup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagPossibleDuplicate

flagPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Remember the new owner under its Idempotency-Key so a repeat replays it instead of duplicating.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: auditEvent

auditEvent:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreatedEvent
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: notifyWelcome

notifyWelcome:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NotifyWelcome
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

All tests pass. The change is complete.

## Summary

The spec required all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) to return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`. Seven escalation handlers were still returning plain `String`/`Map` bodies:

- **400** — `MissingOwnerFieldsHandler` (also fires for the disposable-email and postcode checks, which reuse `MissingOwnerFieldsException`)
- **409** — `CityAtCapacityHandler`, `DuplicateEmailHandler`, `DuplicateHouseholdHandler`, `DuplicateIdentityHandler`, `DuplicateTelephoneHandler`
- **429** — `DailyOwnerLimitHandler`

Each now delegates to the **existing** `ProblemDetails.build(ex, status, detail)` helper and returns `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` — which makes Spring emit `application/problem+json` with all four required members (`type=about:blank`, `title`, `status`, `detail`), status codes unchanged. `MissingOwnerFieldsHandler` additionally preserves its per-field `errors` list as a problem-detail property.

**Keeping structural impact low:** I reused the shared `ProblemDetails` helper rather than writing new formatting logic, so no function grew meaningfully. Every handler class contains exactly one method (WMC_other = 0) and each `handle` method stays cyclomatic-complexity 1 (no branches), so the per-function cost is just the handful of changed lines. I touched only the handler files that genuinely produce the in-scope statuses — the 404/403/500 handlers and the already-compliant `ValidationExceptionHandler` were left untouched.

The `AcceptanceTest` (missing-city → 400 problem+json) and the full suite both build green.
